content.text: Acute Abd:
S/Sx:    -        severe pain     -    N/V       -    hematemesis        -    melena           -    hypotensive       -    peritoneal signs
looks ill            -    pale       -    guarding               -    fever                -    rebound tenderness
Ex.:   -         ruptured appendix        -    ectopic preg      -    Perforation            -    abd trauma w spleen or bowel injury
incarcerated hernia       -    AAA                    -    bowel obstruct      -    bowel ischemia
General Hx: ⍉ acute
HPI: Chloride-PAC
character:     -    pain (sharp, dull, cramp)        -     Distended        -    Bloating         -    achy
Visceral abd pain: gnawing, cramping, aching -> progresses -> sweating, pallor, N/V
pain <- stretch hollow abd organ or wall        ****difficult to localize
From encapsulated organs (liver, spleen) -> capsule gets stretched
somatic (parietal) abd pain: steady achy pain, worse w mvt & coughing
worse than visceral pain                                 **** localized or diffuse
inflam of parietal peritoneum
referred abd pain: non-tender on palpation
pain @distant site: organ & n. innervation = converge on same level of spinal cord
Initial pain site -> ↑intensity -> referred
Location: did pain started somewhere else
Radiation:    -  Aorta: radiates elsewhere    -  Pancreas: radiates elsewhere    -  Appendix: starts else where
Intensity: 3 Q always ask
make abd pain better-worse-same:    1.   Eating?     2.    Vomiting?     3.    BM?
Eating = better: PUD
Eating =worse: GERD
Vomit =better: PUD, bowel obstruction, pancreatitis, gallstone
Vomit = worse: appendicitis, gallstones, pancreatitis, perforation
BM = better: constipation
BM =worse: IBS, Crohns, UC, Hemorrhoids, Fissures
Duration: constant vs intermittent
Stool, Urine, Vomit Q:
Frequency
Color: Melena or hematemesis: GI bleeds
breakdown of hgb proteins by stomach acid
Upper GI bleed:  hgb break down by stomach acids
hematemesis -coffee ground
melena -black tarry
Lower GI bleed: bright red blood in stool hgb
⍉breakdown by stomach acids
Consistency: bristol stool chart
1-2:  constipation
3-4 stools: healthy BM
5-7: Inflam
Blood
smell
Chg from norm: diet, stool, urine. vomit
ROS: 14 Sx
Constipation             -    diarrhea                         -    N/V                           -    early satiety
cramping                   -    passing clot                   -    flank pain                -    Weight gain or loss
Dysuria                      -    urinary frequency        -    Hematuria               -    incontinence
ROS poss from kidneys: uti, pilonephritis, renal infect
Dysphagia: solids, liquids, progressive
Jaundice: 1st appear in sclera & mucosal membranes
Bilirubin Levels:     -    norm: < 1.2 mg/DL      -    visible jaundice: +2.0 - 2.5 mg/DL
Medical Hx
General PMHx
Gastrointestinal dx: GERD, PUD, IBS, pancreatitis    -   major illness   - Hepatitis or cirrhosis   - colorectal CA
GU PMHx
abd or urinary tract injury             -    abd or urinary tract surgery         -    UTIs: how many
menstruation hx: when was 1st day of last period?
*preg in or out of uterus
Poss preg   -    ectopic preg    -   ovarian torsion   -   ovarian cysts
Meds to ask: how much, how often
ASA, NSAIDs: ulcers, bleeding risk
Steroids: ↑acid prod, irritate stomach lining, ulcers, gastritis, pancreatitis
Abx: destroy colon -C. diff, pain, N/V, diarrhea, cramping, flatulence
GLP-1s: side effects =N/V, gastroparesis              *Types: pure GLP-1, Dual GIP-GLP-1, triple agonist
hormone use: ↑malig risk & alter organ function, ↑ pain
Surgery
Gastric surgery:
Gastric bypass: bypasses most of stomach & duodenum
poss lyte imbalances or fat soluble vit deficiencies (EDK)
Adjustable gastric Band (Lap Band): band around stomach -> port under skin
Gastric balloon: inflated balloon in stomach -> easy satiety
Abd or urinary tract surgery or injury
Transition surgery
blood transfusion: poss hep B or C transmission
Immunization:     -   immunization status: Hep A & B
Screening: ever had it?                   -    Hep A:  Exposure               -   Hep B:+18y/o               -   Hep C: All 18 - 79 y/o
Fhx
colorectal CA & familial colorectal CA syndromes  *any CA
gall bladder dz
kidney dz -renal stones, polycystic kidneys
malabsorption -CF, celiac
hirshsprung dz: aganglionic megacolon, congenital & hereditary
⍉enteric ganglion cells in lrg intestine -> functional obstruct
familial mediterranean fever: periodic peritonitis
Complications: amyloidosis, fever, abd pain, chest pain, joint pain
Social Hx
stressful life events: physical & psych chg      -    Traumas    -    exposure to infect      -    travel Hx
ETOH: freq, type, usual amounts                     -   Tobacco       -    substance ->IVDU or cannabis hyperemesis
Nutrition: preferences, religion, involuntary weight gain/loss, chg in diet
Fiber:
Daily Recommended = 25 - 38g
Benefits:
aids gut health                 -
↓ ♡vasc risk -↓lipids, ↓BP, maintain weight
↓DM risk -↑mng
↓risk of  colon CA
weight mng                       -    lipid control                            -   clear plaques
Slow absorb of sugars      -   Soluble fiber feeds microbiome
Foods: less processed = ↑ fiber
Fruits     -   Veggies     -  whole grains   -  Beans     -  Nuts       -  seeds
Gut Microbiome: millions diff flora in gut
Foods: Probiotic rich food, can add prebiotics
Functions:
aids in digestion                -    vit absorb
breakdown waste              -   prod short chain fatty acids
Imbalance Effects:    -   Inflam     -    ↑insulin resistance     -    ↑CV risk     -    eczema
Special Pop
Transitioning:
Surgery Hx        -    Anatomy: AFAB=still do vaginal exam, AMAB =prostate CA
hormone use: ↑malig risk & alter organ function
Anatomy
Quadrants:
RUQ:   -  Liver     -   pancreas (head)    -   gallbladder    -  duodenum     -  pylorus     -  hepatic flexure of colon
LUQ:   -  Lt lobe of liver     -    spleen     -    stomach    -   body & tail pancreas      -     splenic flexure of colon
LLQ:    - descending colon      -   sigmoid colon    -    enlrg=bladder or uterus      -  Lt ureter
Lt spermatic cord or ovary or salpinx / fallopian tube
RLQ:   -  Cecum      -  appendix       -  ascending colon     - terminal ileum     -  enlrg=bladder or uterus
Rt ureter              -   Rt spermatic cord or ovary or salpinx / fallopian tube
GI tract order:
Stomach -> duodenum -> jejunum -> Ileum -> cecum -> appendix
-> ascending colon -> transverse colon -> descending colon -> sigmoid colon -> rectum
Linea Alba and Inguinal Ligament: weak -> ↑hernia location
Peritoneal Spaces:
intraperitoneum: w/in (inside or into) peritoneal cavity
retroperitoneum: behind peritoneum
Primary Organs:   -  Kidneys      -   adrenal glands       -   IVC     -   Ureters       -   abdominal aorta
Secondary Organs:   -   Pancreas      -   duodenum       -   ascending colon     -    descending colon
peritoneum: serious membrane lining abd cavity & cover abd organs
Internal Structures -P.
Kidney: protected by the lower ribs
Kidneys: just below rib 12       -    Rt: lower b/c liver      -    CVA = ribs meets sternum
Physical Exam
Equipment: good light (pen light), drape, gown, pillows, tape measure, marking pen, stethoscope
Special Pop: Transitioning:  anatomy AFAB =still do vaginal exam
B4 Exam:
empty bladder -> get sample     -   ask pain first -location                    -    cut fingernails
observe pt face, ⍉hands           -    help abd relax by supporting knees w pillow or flex knees
Inspection:
